prompt:
EDIT this exact four-part glove sprite sheet into SIMPLE CLOSED MITTENS, showing the BACK OF EACH HAND. Preserve material colors, heraldic drawing style, 2x2 layout, cuff-left orientations and inward grips, but REMOVE ALL FOREARMS, WRISTS AND CUFFS completely. Only the compact hand mass remains.
MANDATORY SHAPE: a rounded mitten silhouette with ONE continuous finger chamber. NO four finger bumps, NO separate finger segments, NO finger grooves, NO individual knuckles, NO articulated finger plates. One broad dorsal metal/leather surface and just a SMALL tucked thumb on the FAR/INNER side of the grip, mostly hidden. No thumb sticking out toward the viewer. The camera sees the back of the mitten, the palm faces away toward the weapon.
TOP LEFT: steel-coloured mitten for gripping a vertical sword/spear handle, wrist end on LEFT, smooth rounded closed finger end on RIGHT, back surface facing viewer. Small curled thumb subtly on UPPER INNER edge, wrapping away, not a thumbs-up. No protruding sleeve, wrist or cuff: trim directly at base of palm.
TOP RIGHT: identical hand/pose in dark warm brown leather.
BOTTOM LEFT: steel mitten supporting a horizontal crossbow stock from below, slightly angled upward to the right, back of hand visible. Smooth single curled finger mass, small inward/far-side thumb. Trim at base of palm, absolutely no wrist or cuff or forearm.
BOTTOM RIGHT: same support mitten in brown leather.
Large simple flat planes, navy silhouette outline, only base/light/shadow, subdued steel-grey and brown leather, no skin. These need to be readable at twenty pixels. Four isolated WHOLE mitten-hand cutouts with transparent gaps, all on actual transparent alpha background. No weapons, no arms, no text, no labels, no cell outlines, no realistic textures, no backgrounds, no shadow. Do not retain anything extending from the hand to the left: that was the unwanted forearm/cuff. Final silhouettes must clearly be HAND-ONLY closed mittens, not gloves with individual fingers.
pose: Hand-only dorsal mittens; no forearms, cuffs or individual fingers. Tucked inward thumb.
